# rust-llama

A native Rust implementation of the functionality in the supplied `llama.cpp-master.zip`.

**This is an active, incomplete port.** The repository builds and runs real pretrained Llama, Qwen2 and Mamba-1 generation plus BERT embedding models on its Rust CPU runtime, including packed Q4 inference. The full frozen-source contract still includes all model architectures, tensor operations, backends, converters, multimodal models, tools, browser features and native clients. Those requirements remain tracked; this checkpoint is not a complete replacement for llama.cpp.

The authoritative source input is the 41,458,461-byte ZIP with SHA-256:

```text
2db1e23f619fcabfd628481683c57b1e3e90db86bd045900a04b6073e1843122
```

Its 4,082 regular files have a complete ownership and hash inventory in [ledger/baseline-files.tsv](ledger/baseline-files.tsv). A path assignment establishes responsibility, not implementation parity. See [current implementation status](docs/PORT_STATUS.md), the [12-track contract](docs/plan.md), and [mandatory release gates](release/gates.tsv).

## Build

Rust 1.99.1 is pinned in `rust-toolchain.toml`. The workspace uses local Cargo path dependencies and no downloaded Cargo packages.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/adybag14-cyber/rust-llama.git
cd rust-llama
rustup toolchain install 1.99.1 --profile minimal --component rustfmt,clippy
cargo build --workspace --release --offline --locked
```

The compiler, platform linker and standard library must already be installed for an offline build. Windows builds use the MSVC toolchain; Linux builds use the native Linux toolchain. No original llama/ggml library, C/C++ project build, Python or Node runtime is part of CPU inference.

## Run a model

Provide a supported GGUF model:

```sh
cargo run --release --offline --locked -p rust-llama-cli -- generate \
  --model /path/to/model.gguf --prompt "Once upon a time" --n-predict 32
```

On PowerShell, put the command on one line. Generated text is written to stdout; token counts and timing are written to stderr.

The high-level generation loader supports dense `llama` models with native SPM or BPE tokenization, full adjacent-pair RoPE without scaling, and F32 KV storage. Dense `qwen2` models add half-pair NeoX RoPE, separate or fused Q/K/V projections, source bias handling, and tied or separate output weights. It also loads Mamba-1 GGUF models with causal convolution, selective recurrent state, optional dt/B/C RMS normalization and tied or separate output weights. Matrix arithmetic implements all 29 weight types in the frozen scalar CPU dot contract, including the K, IQ, ternary and FP4 formats; the [quantization documentation](crates/quant/README.md) lists the precise formats. Unsupported architecture features return an error. A decoder or kernel alone does not establish all-model quality or performance parity.

The runtime retains decoded F32 weights for row access and original packed bytes for native quantized matrix arithmetic. The default decoded-weight budget is 2 GiB; packed storage and runtime/cache allocations are additional. The default context bound is 1,024 tokens and is capped to the model's training limit. Both applications accept the first file of a supported GGUF shard set and automatically discover its declared siblings. The Rust API also accepts explicit ordered paths with cumulative parser limits. Both applications accept `--ctx-size` and `--max-weight-mib`; the pinned Qwen2.5-0.5B Q4_K_M corpus needs `--max-weight-mib 3072` because its decoded F32 row cache exceeds 2 GiB. These are explicit allocation bounds, not total process memory limits. Generation is currently CPU-based; the separately verified CUDA and OpenCL kernel APIs are not yet a complete GPU model backend.

Other CLI commands expose validated GGUF metadata, tokenization, detokenization and per-token logits:

```sh
cargo run --release --offline --locked -p rust-llama-cli -- --help
cargo run --release --offline --locked -p rust-llama-cli -- inspect --model /path/to/model.gguf
cargo run --release --offline --locked -p rust-llama-cli -- tokenize --model /path/to/model.gguf --prompt "Hello"
```

## Encode a BERT sequence

```sh
cargo run --release --offline --locked -p rust-llama-cli -- embed \
  --model /path/to/bert.gguf --prompt "A sentence to encode." --pooling model
```

Dense `bert` GGUF models use the native WordPiece tokenizer and bidirectional encoder. The JSON result includes input token IDs, every raw token embedding and the selected pooled vector. Pooling supports the model default, none, mean, first and last. Vectors are not L2-normalized. Classifier/reranker tensors and other BERT-derived architectures remain explicit unsupported cases.

See the [inference API and model boundaries](crates/inference/README.md).

## Serve completions and embeddings

```sh
cargo run --release --offline --locked -p llama-server -- \
  --model /path/to/model.gguf --bind 127.0.0.1:8080
```

The server connects native/OpenAI text completions and SSE to real Rust inference, with bounded HTTP parsing, cancellation, stop strings and replay. Text chat requires a supported model template. Unsupported request options fail explicitly. Without `--model`, the executable is a diagnostics service and reports inference unavailable.

To serve a supported BERT model's embeddings:

~~~sh
cargo run --release --offline --locked -p llama-server -- \
  --model /path/to/bert.gguf --embeddings --pooling model
~~~

The native /embedding and /embeddings routes preserve pooled or per-token
vectors; /v1/embeddings provides OpenAI shapes, token usage and optional base64
for pooled output. Pooled results use Euclidean normalization by default.
Text, token, mixed and batched inputs follow the frozen server's rules.

See the [server behavior and supported options](crates/llama-server/README.md). This is not full upstream server/browser parity.

## What is implemented

| Area | Executable implementation |
| --- | --- |
| Quantization | All 36 active dtype decoders; all 29 source model quantizers including required/optional importance weights; 32 non-integer codecs including activation and F64 helpers; checked integer setters; all 29 scalar CPU weight dots. |
| Tensors | Checked four-dimensional layouts, immutable shared views, a CPU DAG evaluator, 75 executable operation IDs plus NONE input leaves, all scalar unary/GLU formulas for supported typed families, and 3,240 distinct native graph cases, including convolution, pooling and resize families. |
| Formats and vocabulary | Bounded GGUF v2/v3 reader and owned shard sets, little-endian writer, scalar endian conversion, Llama SPM, BERT WordPiece, BPE with all 64 reachable metadata-selected profiles / 99 aliases, Unigram, RWKV, PLaMo2/PLaMo3, explicit no-vocabulary mode, and exhaustive frozen Unicode/UTF-8 behavior. |
| Model runtime | Llama, Qwen2, Mamba and BERT Rust model graphs from typed weights; contexts, KV/recurrent state, transactions, adapters and state serialization. The GGUF facade loads dense Llama, Qwen2, Mamba-1 and dense BERT. Strict contexts account for owned state and retained checkpoints before mutation. |
| Inference and applications | Pretrained GGUF generation and BERT embeddings, CLI, real-model HTTP/SSE and embedding endpoints, and 184 implemented frozen C API exports. |
| Device foundations | Rust CUDA driver execution and generated PTX kernels; generated OpenCL kernels and execution; typed kernel IR and other backend host foundations. |
| Other imported functionality | Selected native media processing, samplers, chat formatters, separate raw-byte native GBNF and safe character grammar APIs, RPC/CBLAS/DSP utilities and Rust audit/packaging tools. |

Detailed support boundaries are in the crate READMEs and [PORT_STATUS.md](docs/PORT_STATUS.md). Numeric registries, backend probes and example programs are not counted as complete implementations.

## Independent comparisons

Reference C/C++ is built and executed outside this product. Committed fixtures contain data and provenance; runtime crates do not call the reference implementation.

The recorded 9 November 2026 evidence includes:

- **Pretrained F32 inference:** six prompts, 96 matching greedy token IDs and 62,976 compared logits. Matching source accumulation and physical attention-row layout gives bit-identical results against the corresponding Windows and GNU captures.
- **Pretrained Q4_0 inference:** 640,000 unique logits and sixteen greedy IDs match the corresponding original profiles. Packed Q8 activation conversion is retained; the earlier failed all-F32 comparison remains recorded.
- **Pretrained BPE/Q4_K_M inference:** 1,671,168 unique SmolLM2 logits and 24 generated IDs match the corresponding Windows and GNU profiles.
- **Pretrained Mamba-1 inference:** 1,709,520 unique logits and 24 generated IDs match the corresponding original profiles. Three synthetic recurrent models provide ordinary loader and state regressions. Earlier GNU drift remains in the historical evidence.
- **Pretrained Qwen2 inference:** 5,165,824 unique logits and 24 generated IDs match each original profile, with independently captured Q4_K_M weights. Twenty-one synthetic Qwen2 variants cover separate/fused projections, partial biases, output configurations and packed weights. Thirteen physical metadata variants preserve source resolution rules.
- **BERT embeddings:** 13,056 token/pooled values match the corresponding original profiles. The GNU correction preserves the source's four-lane variance reduction. All 122 captured stages of the Windows diagnostic sequence match exactly; 46,080 independent attention outputs remain in the ordinary suite.
- **Sharded loading:** 90 native model/index configurations, including 65 admitted sets and 25 rejections; 64 model configurations compare 464,272 logits/embedding values and 590 greedy IDs per native profile. First-file metadata, per-file tensor origins, cumulative resource limits and retained file handles are checked independently. Ordered streaming split/merge and checkpoint converters remain open.
- **Vocabulary behavior:** the preserved SPM/WordPiece corpora plus 1,499,449 complete BPE vocabulary records across all 14 original BPE models; 5,096 real-model token/piece/detokenization cases; 18,018 GPT-2 alias cases; 23,754 synthetic configuration cases; 22,518 raw-byte cases; 126,896 regex splits. All 64 reachable profiles and 99 aliases are covered on Windows and Linux. Source-inferred special IDs preserve the measured platform container ordering.
- **Remaining tokenizer families:** Unigram, RWKV and PLaMo2/PLaMo3 have 91,476 synthetic family cases, 346,112 original vocabulary records, 10,412 real-vocabulary tokenization cases and 4,067,668 exact normalizer outputs. Invalid source assertion/nonprogress inputs return bounded errors. The no-vocabulary mode is explicit.
- **Unicode behavior:** all 1,114,112 codepoints, 15,957 normalization sequences and 65,809 valid/malformed UTF-8 cases checked against the original source.
- **Quant codecs and dots:** all 36 dtype layouts, exhaustive F16/BF16/F8 patterns, all 29 model quantizers, additional activation/conversion codecs, and complete scalar weight-dot inventory. The weighted/IQ extension adds 3,362 exact original-C encoder rows and 640 native tied-sort cases. Source-undefined payload/access cases have explicit safe behavior documented in the quant crate.
- **Tensor graphs:** 3,240 distinct independently executed frozen GGML graphs. The new convolution/pooling/resize slice adds 981 distinct cases and 530,246 exact output bytes per platform, with exact shapes and strides. Twenty overlapping-gradient cases preserve the measured platform-specific NaN operand order. Indexing compares 599,152 bytes per platform and preserves 88 native MSVC/GNU sort-order differences. The scalar extension checks 256,233 exact outputs, 170,260 transcendental outputs and 96,910 independently rounded high-precision ERF values. A further 1,007 native row/activation/normalization graphs require 2,909,056 exact output bytes per host. Shared scalar/SSE2 row math and the audited system `erff` boundary preserve the exercised dynamic-UCRT/glibc profiles; other providers and remaining ISA policies stay unverified. Independent raw-word gates check 502,058 `erff` and 502,058 scalar quick-GELU inputs per host. Earlier failures and fixed conversion bounds are retained.
- **Actual devices:** 138 CUDA dispatches on RTX 4090 with zero recorded error; OpenCL kernel cases on RTX 4090 and AMD gfx1036 with recorded numerical bounds.
- **C ABI:** 184 of 255 frozen exports, plus four diagnostic extensions, are exercised through independent frozen-header and model harnesses. The latest CPU sampler corpus covers 165 scenarios and 42 real contexts / 585 generated tokens. The BPE/FIM/raw-byte harness compares 1,505,576 vocabulary records and 7,598 tokenization cases. The context/memory extension adds 80 scenarios, 400 checks, 61,440 continuation logits and 1,223,532 native state bytes. The new family getter corpus adds 347,066 vocabulary records and 27,508 tokenization cases; physical metadata adds 23,903 records and 480 outputs across 176 cases. Raw native state restore/reserialization is byte-exact on both platforms; generated Linux floats retain the predeclared numerical budget. Prior core/sampler/WPM fixtures remain passing. The [coverage inventory](crates/ffi/COVERAGE.md) retains all 71 absent exports and the remaining semantic restrictions.
- **Server:** 37 real-model generation requests plus 283 embedding HTTP transcripts per original build (256 tiny-model, 27 pretrained BGE). Both verified profiles require exact corresponding F32 bits and all seven base64 vectors. Direct normalization checks cover another 4,608 values. Real TCP lifecycle tests cover configured load bounds, limits, provider failures, disconnects, shutdown and complete deadline errors.

The original MSVC and GNU builds do not use identical row arithmetic: the verified GNU build enables source SSE2 exponentiation, reductions and variance, while the verified MSVC build uses scalar rows. Separate expected captures preserve those differences. Test expectations select their profile independently of runtime dispatch. The model runtime also preserves 256-column attention padding and physical cache holes. None of these results establishes every CPU instruction-set path.

Evidence and qualifications are under [evidence/2026-11-09](evidence/2026-11-09). These results establish the exercised configurations, not all hardware, models or performance parity. Pretrained weights are not distributed in this repository; the tokenizer-only GGUF is test data with provenance.

## Verify

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test --workspace --all-targets --offline --locked
cargo test --workspace --all-targets --release --offline --locked
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --offline --locked -- -D warnings
cargo xtask audit
cargo xtask fixtures
```

Windows and Linux CI run these checks and separately download hash-pinned F32, Q4_0, BPE/Q4_K_M, Qwen2, Mamba-1 and BERT model inputs for explicit numerical comparisons. Hardware/vendor tests retain their own explicit prerequisites. The corresponding verified original profiles produce exact results for the exercised model cases; unchanged portable error budgets remain available for unverified targets. See [fixtures/inference/README.md](fixtures/inference/README.md), [quant validation](crates/quant/README.md), [tensor validation](crates/tensor/README.md) and [xtask commands](xtask/README.md).

With the frozen source extracted separately:

```sh
cargo xtask verify-source /path/to/llama.cpp-master
```

`cargo xtask release-check` deliberately fails while any mandatory full-port gate remains open.

## Provenance and license

The integration reuses and audits the supplied T05–T08 and T09–T12 Rust progress archives. Their hashes and imported files are recorded in [docs/imports/manifest.json](docs/imports/manifest.json). Historical reports are preserved under `docs/imports/`; current claims require current evidence.

Original project code is MIT licensed. Original ggml attribution is retained in [LICENSE-UPSTREAM](LICENSE-UPSTREAM) and [NOTICE](NOTICE). Component notices identify separately licensed adapted code, including the native tied-sort helpers. Fixture provenance records additional source identities and qualifications.

# Current port status

Updated 9 November 2026. The user objective remains a complete native Rust port of the frozen ZIP. **The full port is not complete.** This document records actual executable scope and the work still required. No overall completion percentage is assigned.

## Source and product boundary

The baseline ZIP SHA-256 is `2db1e23f619fcabfd628481683c57b1e3e90db86bd045900a04b6073e1843122`. All 4,082 source paths have an owner, byte count and checksum in `ledger/baseline-files.tsv`. Source verification compares the complete extracted tree, including additions and removals. Ownership coverage is not semantic completion.

The product's maintained implementation is Rust. Frozen C/C++ reference builds, model downloads and oracle generators remain outside the repository. Numeric tables, tokenizer-only GGUF, reference float/byte arrays, media examples and synthetic binary parser inputs are declared fixture data. Minimal Cargo/CI configuration, licenses and documentation retain their actual formats.

The merged workspace has local path dependencies. Optional OS/driver/vendor interfaces remain named external boundaries. They do not import the original llama.cpp implementation. See `release/dependency-inventory.tsv`.

## Pretrained inference findings

The first end-to-end model is `stories260K.gguf`, SHA-256 `270cba1bd5109f42d03350f60406024560464db173c0e387d91f0426d3bd256d`. The independent frozen llama API oracle uses one CPU thread, F32 KV and disabled flash attention. Six prompts produced 96 matching greedy tokens. The initial 62,976-logit comparison had maximum absolute error `1.764297485e-5`. Matching the source's F32 products with F64 accumulation gave exact Windows equality and left a historical GNU difference of `5.722045898e-6`. The new matching-profile captures and physical attention-row correction now give exact equality on both verified targets. The predefined portable bound `2e-4 + 2e-5 * abs(reference)` is unchanged.

The larger `stories15M-q4_0.gguf`, SHA-256 `66967fbece6dbe97886593fdbb73589584927e29119ec31f08090732d1861739`, initially exposed a real bug: expanding all packed matrices to F32 preserved sixteen greedy tokens but changed logits by as much as `0.4481242895126343`. The corrected runtime retains packed weights, converts activations according to the source CPU trait, and evaluates integer block dots with the original scaling order. All 640,000 compared logits then matched the frozen Windows reference exactly. The report before the fix is retained beside the report after the fix.

The F16 BGE-small BERT model, SHA-256 `f0b2fef971e8366438bfd2d9aefea1b0115919389448806d290237f638bae999`, exposed a second real rounding issue. Input embeddings, normalization and Q/K/V projections were exact, but F32 attention accumulation differed from the scalar source's F64 sum. Those small differences crossed GELU table bins in later layers. Correcting attention and mean-pooling order yields exact Windows equality for all 13,056 compared values and all 122 captured diagnostic stages. The earlier GNU comparison had maximum error `1.348853111e-4`, within the original fixed tolerance. Preserving the GNU source's four-lane variance order and comparing its separate native capture now gives exact equality. A 12-layer independent attention fixture exercises 46,080 output values in ordinary tests. The before/after diagnosis remains recorded.

The equivalent big-endian BERT download is separately hash-pinned and produces the same expected results through the Rust reader. The frozen C reader rejects that opposite-endian file; this is reader validation against the equivalent little-endian native corpus, not a claim of original-reader support.

Exact equality is recorded evidence for the exercised build and prompt, against the corresponding original profile. Portable tests retain the previously declared numerical tolerance because platform math libraries and ISA reduction orders can differ. These tests do not establish arbitrary quantized-format support or all-model quality parity.

The SPM corpus uses the original vocabulary-only fixture and verifies 68 cases, 312 pieces, parsing/insertion flags, byte fallback, whitespace and detokenization. WordPiece adds 1,728 native cases across nine metadata variants, all 30,522 original vocabulary entries and 72 special-token fallback cases. Unicode checks cover all 1,114,112 codepoints, 15,957 normalization sequences and 65,809 UTF-8 inputs. The BPE extension now covers every reachable metadata profile: 64 pretokenizer types and 99 aliases. Three other enum names have no metadata dispatch in the frozen source; they are not invented as extra supported profiles. Independent Windows/Linux comparisons cover all 14 original BPE vocabularies, complete property/piece/EOG records, 22,518 raw-byte cases and 126,896 regex splits. Ambiguous inferred EOT/FIM IDs preserve the measured MSVC/libstdc++ container ordering. Full-vector/input tests require explicit original-vocabulary prerequisites; compact synthetic native corpora run ordinarily. The remaining frozen tokenizer families are now implemented: Unigram, RWKV and PLaMo2/PLaMo3, with an explicit no-vocabulary metadata mode. Their independent corpus covers 91,476 synthetic cases, 346,112 original vocabulary records, 10,412 real-vocabulary tokenization cases and 4,067,668 normalizer outputs. This does not close conversion, sharding or every native C override configuration.

## Scalar codecs, native behavior and HTTP extensions

The scalar codec slice now covers every defined source model quantizer, including
importance-weighted legacy/K/IQ fitting. Three model formats require caller-supplied
weights. Q8_1/Q8_K remain activation codecs and F64 remains a conversion helper;
they are not counted as extra source model quantizers. The new independent corpus
has 3,362 original-C encoded rows and 640 tied-sort cases. The original IQ4_NL
uninitialized near-zero payload and exceptional IQ1 out-of-bounds fallback are
handled explicitly and excluded from undefined-source byte parity claims.

The raw-byte GBNF engine remains separate from the safe Unicode recognizer. Its
native corpus checks 383,053 candidate masks and source token terminals/partial
byte behavior. The C sampler extension adds strict/lazy grammar, DRY, adaptive-p
and infill, with 165 independent scenarios and 42 real contexts / 585 generated
tokens. Candidate order, flags, float bits, selected indices and lifecycle
operations match the frozen Windows DLL. Native BPE/FIM getter, piece and
detokenization checks add 1,505,576 vocabulary records and 7,598 tokenization cases.
The context/memory extension raises the implemented inventory to 184 exported source symbols; 71 remain absent. Its independent 80-case cohort covers 400 checks, 61,440 continuation logits and 1,223,532 state bytes. Restoring and reserializing original state payloads is byte-exact on both platforms. Windows generated floats are exact; Linux retains the original fixed tolerance. Native sessions, per-sequence state, memory operations, bounded copies and file edge cases have separate frozen-header checks. An additional family C getter cohort covers 347,066 vocabulary records and 27,508 tokenization cases, with 176 physical-metadata cases covering 23,903 records and 480 outputs. Nonnull metadata override lists and native recurrent C memory remain explicitly unsupported.

The server embedding corpora exercise 256 ordinary tiny-model requests and
27 explicit pretrained BGE requests per original build. Both verified profiles
now require exact corresponding F32 bits and all seven base64 vectors. GNU
expectations come from a separately built, unmodified original server. The
original profiles themselves differ in 23,786 of 24,704 embedding values; mode
0 amplifies their maximum absolute difference to 1.4208984375. That source-to-
source difference is not a Rust error. The matching-profile Rust comparisons
record zero error. Earlier cross-profile failures and the unchanged portable
normalization envelope remain recorded. Direct normalization of identical raw
inputs is separately checked over 4,608 outputs.

Transport failure tests exposed a deadline race: the listener's monitor could
cancel the worker before the handler checked its timer, turning a timeout into
a dropped response. Both embedding and nonstream generation now check the
deadline before forwarding a generic cancellation result. The regression
requires a complete HTTP 504 response and verifies that capacity is released.
Disconnect and server-shutdown cancellation remain separate cases.

## Qwen2, source row math and tensor coverage

Dense Qwen2 execution supports half-pair NeoX RoPE without scaling, separate or
fused Q/K/V projections, source bias selection, tied or separate output and
output bias. The pinned Qwen2.5-0.5B Q4_K_M input contributes 5,165,824 unique
logits and 24 greedy predictions per original profile. Both profiles match
their own native output exactly. Its decoded F32 cache requires a 3 GiB weight
budget; the default 2 GiB limit deliberately rejects the load.

Twenty-one synthetic Qwen2 variants cover separate/fused projection and bias
combinations, packed Q4 and output variants. Thirteen physical metadata inputs
check source typing and RoPE resolution. Review caught partial fused-bias
selection and nonfinite output-bias transaction failures; permanent regressions
and the failed baselines are retained.

The verified original GNU build enables SSE2 row exponentiation, four-lane
sum and variance; verified MSVC uses scalar row branches. Rust preserves those
policies, whole-row SiLU, attention padding to 256 columns, masked cache holes
and shared attention widths across active streams. Expected profile selection
is independent of runtime dispatch. Native physical-layout probes include
31,744 continuation logits and 193,868 state bytes, exact on both hosts.
Unverified ISA and platform configurations remain open.

The convolution/pooling/resize extension adds thirteen operation IDs and
981 distinct original graphs, including 530,246 exact output bytes per host.
Twenty overlapping backward-gradient cases preserve native MSVC/GNU NaN
operand selection; the earlier GNU mismatch in ten cases and 66 F32 words is
retained in the evidence.
Shape, stride and parameter/error behavior are tested separately. Tensor
coverage is now 75 executable IDs plus NONE, with 26 operation IDs still
pending. Across the tensor corpus there are 3,240 distinct graph inputs and
6,118 native captures; repeated platform executions are not counted as new
graph cases. Shared scalar/SSE2 row math now serves model-runtime and tensor;
1,007 additional original graphs require exact matching-profile bytes. The
system erff boundary is independently verified on the captured x86_64 dynamic
UCRT/glibc profiles; other providers, static targets and remaining ISA behavior
retain explicit unverified or fallback qualifications.

## Memory and execution qualifications

The high-level model facade loads a single dense Llama, Qwen2, Mamba-1 or BERT GGUF into host memory. Non-matrix vectors are decoded F32. Matrices retain a decoded F32 row-access cache and, for supported non-F32 types, the original packed bytes needed for native dot arithmetic. The decoded-weight limit is not a total process memory limit. Loader hparams use the source UINT32/FLOAT32 types and 512-layer maximum; split.count uses UINT16 and accepts omitted, zero or one for a single file. Unsupported NextN/MTP, PRISM transforms, scaled RoPE and noncausal decoder modes return explicit errors. There is no mmap, tensor streaming, GPU model placement or full asynchronous scheduler claim.

Llama and Qwen2 decoder context state uses F32 KV. Mamba-1 owns F32 causal-convolution and selective-SSM state; cancellation and state restoration are transactional through the strict Rust Context API. Native C recurrent-memory compatibility remains separately open. BERT uses complete bidirectional sequences and its trained position table; it has no decoder KV context through this facade. Model instances are immutable and shared; each generation request owns independent context and sampler state. Stop strings and incomplete UTF-8 suffixes are withheld across token boundaries. Errors and cancellation do not commit partial model state. The C ABI documentation separately states accepted/rejected native parameter configurations.

The strict Rust Context defaults to a 1 GiB max_state_bytes budget. It reserves
owned sequence/layer records, KV and recurrent capacities, planning records,
transactional state and retained checkpoints before mutation. checkpoint() and
ContextCheckpoint::try_clone() return errors on allocation/budget failures.
Reservations survive a dropped context; cross-context restore charges the
destination. The contract excludes model weights, execution scratch, returned
logits/embeddings, caller buffers and allocator overhead. Serialization charges
the output while constructing it, then transfers ownership to the caller.

NativeContext uses a separate budget. Its earlier full-batch KV correction is
retained; review additionally accounted for temporary stream/chunk descriptors
and resident outer-vector storage. A regression rejects the old underestimated
budget atomically and succeeds at the sufficient budget; removing only that
descriptor charge makes the regression fail. Neither state budget is an RSS
limit. Default F16 C-API cache modes and the complete original worker/flash
configuration remain unimplemented.

The CLI and server accept --ctx-size and --max-weight-mib, and the server
exposes RuntimeProvider::load_with_options for the same checked limits.
Generation currently supports greedy or temperature/distribution sampling with an explicit u32 seed. The presence of other sampler implementations in the behavior crate does not mean every upstream generation option is wired into the CLI/server.

# GGUF inference facade

This crate connects checked GGUF loading, native tokenizers and the Rust model runtime. It has no dependency on an original llama/ggml binary and does not invoke a reference executable.

## Executable model scope

| GGUF architecture | Tokenizer | Current high-level execution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `llama` | Llama SentencePiece or native BPE | Dense autoregressive generation and complete per-token logits, standard adjacent-pair RoPE without scaling, F32 KV state. |
| `qwen2` | Native BPE | Dense generation and complete logits, half-pair NeoX RoPE without scaling, separate or fused Q/K/V with source bias rules, F32 KV state. |
| `bert` | BERT WordPiece | Dense bidirectional encoding, complete token embeddings and none/mean/first/last pooling. |
| `mamba` | Native tokenizer metadata; SPM and BPE independently exercised | Mamba-1 causal convolution and selective recurrence, tied or separate output weights, optional unweighted dt/B/C RMS normalization. |

Mamba-1 loading validates source tensor names and dimensions before constructing its owned recurrent state. Convolution and SSM A tensors require the source CPU kernel's F32 storage. The frozen loader does not load optional dt/B/C normalization weight tensors; its metadata flag selects unweighted normalization. Other architectures, unsupported tensor arrangements and unimplemented options return explicit errors. The full upstream architecture and runtime contract remains open.

All 29 weight types supported by the frozen scalar CPU dot contract are accepted by the matrix loader. This establishes the available matrix arithmetic, not quality validation for every combination of architecture and quantization. The pretrained corpus exercises F32 and Q4_0 Llama, BPE/Q4_K_M SmolLM2, Q4_K_M Qwen2, F16 Mamba-1 and F16 BERT.

## Loading and memory

`Model::load` uses a 2 GiB decoded F32 weight budget and a requested context of 1,024 tokens, capped to the training context. `Model::load_with_options` lets the caller set those limits. The pinned Qwen2.5-0.5B Q4_K_M model has a separate output matrix and a decoded cache larger than 2 GiB; its comparisons use a 3 GiB weight budget and context 128.

The single-path APIs automatically discover declared GGUF siblings. The Rust
`Model::load_from_splits` and `load_from_splits_with_options` APIs take explicit
ordered paths; `Model::load_from_gguf` consumes a validated `GgufSet`. Primary
metadata is authoritative, tensor names are globally unique, and each tensor
retains its own file offset and byte order. Limits apply cumulatively across
the set. The decoded-weight allowance covers every tensor before decoding.
Missing or malformed siblings fail transactionally. The [GGUF documentation](../gguf/README.md)
describes filename rules, safe input bounds and the remaining converter/writer work.

Matrices retain decoded F32 values for row access. Supported non-F32 matrices also retain their packed representation so multiplication preserves the original activation conversion and scaling order. The decoded-weight budget does not include packed bytes, activations, KV state, tokenizer data or other allocations. Loading is into host memory; there is no mmap or GPU model placement claim.

The GGUF reader handles little- and big-endian scalar values. F16 and BF16 packed matrix words are converted to the Rust kernel's byte order; F8 requires no word swap. Other big-endian packed arithmetic remains unsupported.

The strict `llama_model_runtime::Context` separately defaults to a 1 GiB `max_state_bytes` budget. Checked reservations cover owned sequence/layer records, KV or recurrent float capacities, planning records, transactional state and retained checkpoints. `checkpoint()` and `ContextCheckpoint::try_clone()` are fallible. Reservations can outlive the context; restoring into another context charges the destination. The budget excludes model weights, execution scratch, returned logits/embeddings, caller buffers and allocator overhead. Serialized output is charged while being constructed, then becomes caller-owned. Native C-compatible `NativeContext` has a distinct resource contract.

## Generation

`generate` creates an independent context and sampler for each call. Its explicit options are a token budget, temperature, u32 seed and stop strings. Temperature zero selects greedy decoding. Output callbacks receive UTF-8 text, with incomplete byte sequences and potential stop-string suffixes withheld across token boundaries.

`logits_for_tokens` returns every vocabulary logit after each supplied token. It is intended for consumers that require raw logits and for independent conformance comparisons.

`runtime_model()` returns `Result<Arc<llama_model_runtime::Model>>`. It rejects an embedding-only executor. Call `supports_generation()` when selecting a task; successful GGUF loading alone does not imply generation capability.

## Dense BERT embeddings

`embed_tokens(tokens, pooling, cancel)` returns:

- `tokens`: one raw embedding vector per input token.
- `pooled`: no vector for `Pooling::None`, the first or last token for those modes, or the source mean-pooling operation.

`embed(text, pooling_override, cancel)` applies the model's WordPiece tokenizer and insertion rules before encoding. An omitted override uses the GGUF pooling metadata; absent metadata preserves the source default of no pooling. The BGE model in the corpus selects its first/CLS token.

Vectors are **not L2-normalized**. The CLI reports `normalized: false`. Consumers that require cosine-normalized vectors must perform that separate operation.

All tokens in a sequence can attend to all other tokens. Position indices default to their sequence indices, and token types follow the frozen BERT graph's row-zero rule. Requested context limits are checked without truncating the trained position-embedding table. Empty sequences, out-of-range token IDs, excessive context and cancellation return errors.

Classifier/reranker tensors, Nomic/Jina/other BERT-derived architectures, causal BERT variants, MoE and unimplemented graph features are rejected. BERT does not provide autoregressive logits or generation through this facade.

## CLI examples

```sh
cargo run --release --offline --locked -p rust-llama-cli -- generate --model /path/to/llama.gguf --prompt "Once upon a time" --n-predict 32
cargo run --release --offline --locked -p rust-llama-cli -- generate --model /path/to/qwen2.gguf --max-weight-mib 3072 --ctx-size 128 --prompt "Once upon a time" --n-predict 8
cargo run --release --offline --locked -p rust-llama-cli -- embed --model /path/to/bert.gguf --prompt "A sentence to encode." --pooling model
cargo run --release --offline --locked -p rust-llama-cli -- embed --model /path/to/bert.gguf --tokens 101,1037,6251,102 --pooling mean
```

The embedding JSON contains model identity, input token IDs, dimensions, pooling mode, every token vector and the optional pooled vector.

# Bounded GGUF files and model shards

The crate reads seekable GGUF v2/v3 files, validates their metadata and tensor
directories, and reads tensor payloads on demand. It also owns complete GGUF
shard sets using the frozen original model loader's rules. All maintained
implementation is Rust; no original llama/ggml binary or foreign executable is
called at runtime.

This is a formats and loading slice of T04. It does not implement the frozen
checkpoint converters, the ordered streaming split/merge applications, or every
format compatibility edge.

## Single files and shard sets

Gguf<R: Read + Seek> remains the single-file parser. Gguf<File>::open and
open_with_limits open local files. Public metadata and descriptors retain their
serialized value types, dimensions, dtype IDs and offsets. read_tensor returns
stored bytes, while read_f32 performs checked supported dtype decoding.

GgufSet opens one primary path and retains every file handle used during
validation. It has one primary metadata map and a unified tensor directory.
Each tensor is associated with its actual file, data offset and byte order.
Reading a tensor does not reopen its path. Replacing a directory entry after
opening cannot silently redirect a later read to a different file.

| API | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| GgufSet::open(path) | Open a single file or discover its declared siblings. |
| GgufSet::open_with_limits(path, limits) | Same behavior with explicit cumulative parser and shard limits. |
| GgufSet::open_splits(paths) | Open a caller-supplied ordered list using default limits. |
| GgufSet::open_splits_with_limits(paths, limits) | Explicit list and explicit limits. |
| metadata() | Primary metadata only. Subsidiary model metadata is never merged. |
| tensors(), tensor(name) | Complete descriptor-order list and indexed lookup by unique name. |
| tensor_shard(name), tensor_endian(name) | Tensor's originating file and payload byte order. |
| shard_info(index) | File path, version, endian, alignment, data offset, length, count and header usage. |
| read_tensor(name), read_f32(name) | Fallible payload reads through the retained file handle. |
| file_bytes() | Sum of physical file sizes, including headers, padding and trailing bytes. |
| tensor_bytes(), tensor_elements() | Unified stored payload bytes and logical element count. |
| header_usage() | Cumulative charged header bytes, metadata entries, values and tensor descriptors. |

Construction is transactional: a malformed or missing shard releases all staged
file owners and returns an error. No partially indexed set is published.
Tensor payload decoding remains lazy; opening does not concatenate the model
or eagerly decode its weights. Header parsing uses one temporary read-ahead
buffer, bounded to 64 KiB and to the remaining file/header allowance. This can
prefetch a bounded payload prefix. The buffer is discarded and the reader is
returned to its consumed logical position before it is retained for later
payload reads.

## Frozen model loader rules

These rules follow src/llama-model-loader.cpp and the original llama C API.
They deliberately differ from some stricter checks performed by the original
standalone merge application.

1. Primary split.count is UINT16. An omitted value, zero or one selects the
   ordinary single-file path. For this case, additional explicit paths are
   ignored, including paths that do not exist, as in the original API.
2. When the primary count exceeds one, primary split.no must be UINT16 zero.
   An explicit path list must contain exactly the declared number of files.
   Oversized explicit lists are checked without reproducing the original
   narrowing cast to UINT16.
3. Automatic discovery requires the exact suffix
   -00001-of-000NN.gguf for the primary file. Siblings use the same prefix and
   one-based, minimum-width-five decimal numbers. The first split must be
   selected. Native path representations are preserved, including Unicode on
   Windows and non-UTF-8 names on Unix.
4. Subsidiary file i must have UINT16 split.no equal to i. This is the only
   subsidiary model metadata key used by the original file-set loader.
   Subsidiary architecture, tokenizer, split.count and total-count values do
   not replace or augment primary model metadata. Each file's GGUF header and
   general.alignment still undergo format validation.
5. Tensor names must be unique across all files. Primary split.tensors.count
   must be a nonnegative INT32 equal to the complete tensor count.
6. A metadata-only first shard is valid. Every later tensor offset uses its own
   file's data section, even when header lengths and alignments differ.

The original merge tool also compares subsidiary split.count and writes a
single-file output with split.count reset to zero. This loader does not apply
those merge-tool-only checks.

## Parser layout details

The frozen GGUF reader requires tensor offsets to equal the cumulative padded
payload size in descriptor order. Aligned gaps, overlaps and reordered payload
regions are rejected. Every absolute file offset, payload end, dimension product
and cumulative count uses checked arithmetic.

Zero-dimensional tensors represent one scalar. Zero-element dimensions and
empty tensor names are accepted where the original format reader accepts them;
names of 64 or more bytes are rejected. Dimensions and products remain inside
the signed GGML domain. Model vector/matrix shape checks pad serialized
dimensions with trailing ones, matching original GGML shape resolution.

When a file has no tensors, the original reader reports the unpadded end of
its header as data_offset. The original writer still pads its output.
Both padded and unpadded metadata-only inputs are therefore valid. A nonempty
tensor directory uses the aligned data-section offset.

The raw original no_alloc GGUF reader can accept a truncated tensor payload
because it only parses the header. The original model loader rejects that file.
The Rust parser checks payload bounds during opening and rejects it earlier;
the native test corpus records this distinction explicitly.

The existing Rust reader also supports opposite-endian scalar GGUF decoding.
The frozen original C reader rejects the opposite-endian file, so that extension
is not described as native reader acceptance. Packed matrix endian support
remains limited to the forms explicitly handled by the inference loader.

The metadata representation currently requires UTF-8 strings and rejects NUL
keys/names. Full arbitrary-byte metadata compatibility remains open.

## Resource limits

ShardLimits contains max_shards and the existing Limits value. The defaults are:

| Limit | Default | Accounting |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Owned files | 1,024 | Complete shard set |
| Header bytes, including required alignment | 256 MiB | Sum across all shards |
| Metadata entries | 100,000 | Sum across all shards |
| Metadata values | 4,000,000 | Sum across all shards |
| Tensor descriptors | 100,000 | Sum across all shards |
| One string | 16 MiB | Each string |
| One array | 1,000,000 values | Each array |
| One stored/decoded tensor read | 2 GiB | Each requested read |

Limits are resource policy, not new GGUF field widths. Callers can select
different bounds explicitly. Each subsidiary parser receives the remaining
cumulative allowances, so a declared split count cannot multiply the default
header budget.

Before reserving a descriptor or metadata-value vector, the parser checks its
minimum possible encoded length against both the remaining file and the
remaining header allowance. This prevents an attacker-controlled count from
reserving a large vector before the first later byte charge fails. Owned vector
and file-set reservations use checked, fallible allocation APIs.

These limits bound format work and payload reads. They are not a total-process
memory budget. Metadata tree allocation overhead, temporary decode buffers,
model weights and runtime state have separate costs. The model facade's decoded
weight budget counts every tensor from every shard before decoding any weights.

## High-level model integration

The existing Model::load and Model::load_with_options paths automatically use
GgufSet. Dense Llama, dense Qwen2, Mamba-1 and dense BERT keep their existing
runtime graph and arithmetic paths. CLI and server calls that already use
Model::load inherit automatic sibling discovery.

The additional Rust facade APIs are:

- Model::load_from_splits(paths)
- Model::load_from_splits_with_options(paths, options)
- Model::load_from_gguf(files, options)

The last form consumes a previously validated GgufSet, allowing applications to
choose parser and file-count limits before model loading. No new C ABI exports
or native split-filename buffer conventions are claimed by this slice.

For example, a consumer can open explicit files with a 64-file limit:

~~~rust
use llama_gguf::{GgufSet, ShardLimits};
use llama_inference::{LoadOptions, Model};

let paths = ["part-a.gguf", "part-b.gguf"];
let limits = ShardLimits {
    max_shards: 64,
    ..ShardLimits::default()
};
let files = GgufSet::open_splits_with_limits(&paths, limits)?;
let model = Model::load_from_gguf(files, &LoadOptions::default())?;
~~~

Low-level malformed-file and resource errors remain distinct GGUF errors.
The high-level inference facade preserves its existing error mapping.

## Independent corpus

The committed shard inputs and expected outputs originate from the frozen
GGUF parser, original gguf-split executable, original writer/quantizers and
original model C APIs. Captures were completed on MSVC x64 and GNU x64 before
the first Rust shard-model comparison. Reference implementations, capture
programs and pretrained weights remain outside the product.

The six fixtures under fixtures/gguf contain:

| File | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| shards-reference.json | Case decisions, requests, native metadata, shapes, offsets, IDs, pieces and byte-pool references. |
| shards-inputs.bin | 132 distinct native/synthetic GGUF inputs, materialized at 187 case paths. |
| shards-payloads.bin | Exact independently extracted native tensor payload bytes. |
| shards-msvc-values.f32le.bin | Lossless MSVC model/embedding F32 expected values. |
| shards-gnu-values.f32le.bin | Independent GNU model/embedding F32 expected values. |
| shards-provenance.json | Source, generator, model-origin, library, raw capture and artifact identities. |

There are 90 model/index configurations: 65 complete file sets are accepted,
25 are rejected, and 64 supported model configurations execute. Ten additional
raw format cases cover scalar/empty/name/layout boundaries. The models include
F32 and packed Llama, BERT token embeddings and pooling, Mamba default/RMS/untied
graphs, and Qwen2 separate/fused-Q4/untied-output graphs. Ordinary and
metadata-only-first splits execute through both automatic and explicit APIs.

The ordinary regression verifies structural acceptance, primary-only metadata,
each file origin, exact tensor bytes, 464,272 model/embedding values and 590
greedy IDs over those executions. Repeated paths do not count as new models or
unique numerical rows. Expected pools remove only byte-identical duplicate
records and a verified final-prompt/first-greedy overlap.

Token IDs, bytes and structural decisions are exact. The two verified x86_64 MSVC/GNU targets require identical F32 bits.
Other targets use the existing 2e-4 + 2e-5 * abs(reference) portability budget
selected before the first Rust shard evaluation. Existing architecture-specific
suites and stricter criteria remain unchanged. Expected profile selection is independent
of runtime dispatch.

Additional tests verify cumulative budgets, payload-read laziness, aggregate
decoded-weight limits, retained file-handle identity, Unicode discovery and
Unix non-UTF-8 paths. The two early-reservation regressions were independently
replayed with only their preflight calls removed; both fail in that negative

~~~sh
cargo test --offline --locked -p llama-gguf -p llama-inference --all-targets
cargo test --release --offline --locked -p llama-gguf -p llama-inference --all-targets
cargo clippy --offline --locked -p llama-gguf -p llama-inference --all-targets -- -D warnings
~~~

Existing hash-pinned pretrained inference comparisons run separately on both
verified targets. Their numerical data and tolerances are not regenerated.

## Bounded metadata I/O

The original stdio reader buffers small header reads. Passing a File directly
to the Rust scalar parser caused each length, scalar and token string to reach
the backing file separately. The corrected header adapter allocates at most
64 KiB through a fallible reservation. Refills cannot exceed the remaining
physical file or metadata allowance. It preserves short reads and I/O errors,
rewinds unused read-ahead on both parse success and failure, and leaves the
public Gguf<R> owner and payload seek path unchanged.

A header-only measurement on the pinned Qwen2.5-0.5B file through WSL /mnt/c
recorded 760,618 underlying File reads and 100.5658 seconds before buffering,
versus 93 reads and 0.07945 seconds afterward. Both parsed 26 metadata entries,
455,285 values, 291 tensors and 5,947,744 charged header bytes. The buffered run
read a further 16,043 bytes into its bounded temporary buffer and then restored
the logical cursor. It did not decode weights.

These are single-run measurements of this mounted filesystem and its current
cache/load conditions. They do not establish general CPU, disk or model
throughput. The deterministic read-count regression, budget checks, partial-read
and injected-I/O-error tests establish the implementation behavior separately
from timing. Existing decoder CLI evidence preserves the original 90-95 second
Qwen loads; native numerical references remain unchanged.

## Remaining format and conversion work

The existing writer emits little-endian GGUF from a sorted metadata map and
borrowed tensor payloads. It is not an ordered streaming source-equivalent
split/merge writer. An ordered metadata representation and a bounded streaming
payload writer are needed before those tools can preserve original output
ordering and handle large transformations faithfully.

Local Safetensors/index loading, architecture-specific checkpoint conversion,
tokenizer/config translation, quantization application policy, PyTorch inputs,
LoRA and multimodal conversion, remote range loading and remaining metadata
utilities are still separate full-port requirements. Sharded model execution
does not close T04 or the overall port.

Implementation follows the supplied llama.cpp/ggml MIT-licensed source. Preserve
LICENSE-UPSTREAM and NOTICE; fixture provenance identifies inherited model
vocabulary metadata and the deterministic synthetic weight generators.

jobs:
  cpu:
    name: CPU / ${{ matrix.os }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, windows-latest]
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    timeout-minutes: 30
    env:
      CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
      RUST_BACKTRACE: 1
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Install pinned compiler and review tools
        run: rustup toolchain install 1.99.1 --profile minimal --component rustfmt,clippy
      - name: Formatting
        run: cargo fmt --all -- --check
      - name: Debug tests
        run: cargo test --workspace --all-targets --offline --locked
      - name: Release tests
        run: cargo test --workspace --all-targets --release --offline --locked
      - name: Strict Clippy
        run: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --offline --locked -- -D warnings
      - name: Source and dependency audit
        run: cargo run --offline --locked -p xtask -- audit
      - name: Windows system math file identity
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        run: cargo run --offline --locked -p xtask -- hash "$env:SystemRoot\System32\ucrtbase.dll"
      - name: GNU system math file identity
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: cargo run --offline --locked -p xtask -- hash /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libm.so.6
      - name: Independent fixture integrity
        run: cargo run --offline --locked -p xtask -- fixtures
      - name: Release build
        run: cargo build --workspace --release --offline --locked
      - name: Fetch pinned F32 model data
        run: curl --fail --location --ipv4 --retry 3 --output "${{ runner.temp }}/stories260K.gguf" https://huggingface.co/ggml-org/models-moved/resolve/main/tinyllamas/stories260K.gguf
      - name: Fetch pinned Q4 model data
        run: curl --fail --location --ipv4 --retry 3 --output "${{ runner.temp }}/stories15M-q4_0.gguf" https://huggingface.co/ggml-org/models-moved/resolve/main/tinyllamas/stories15M-q4_0.gguf
      - name: Fetch pinned BERT model data
        run: curl --fail --location --ipv4 --retry 3 --output "${{ runner.temp }}/bert-bge-small-f16.gguf" https://huggingface.co/ggml-org/models-moved/resolve/main/bert-bge-small/ggml-model-f16.gguf
      - name: Fetch equivalent big-endian BERT model data
        run: curl --fail --location --ipv4 --retry 3 --output "${{ runner.temp }}/bert-bge-small-f16-big-endian.gguf" https://huggingface.co/ggml-org/models-moved/resolve/main/bert-bge-small/ggml-model-f16-big-endian.gguf
      - name: Fetch pinned BPE Q4_K model data
        run: curl --fail --location --ipv4 --retry 3 --output "${{ runner.temp }}/SmolLM2-135M-Q4_K_M.gguf" https://huggingface.co/ggml-org/SmolLM2-135M-GGUF/resolve/main/SmolLM2-135M-Q4_K_M.gguf
      - name: Fetch pinned Mamba recurrent model data
        run: curl --fail --location --ipv4 --retry 3 --output "${{ runner.temp }}/mamba-130m-hf.f16.gguf" https://huggingface.co/mradermacher/mamba-130m-hf-GGUF/resolve/ecd441bd76c60ebf9c3e71bfc3f83ba64fa1edd1/mamba-130m-hf.f16.gguf
      - name: Fetch pinned Qwen2 Q4_K model data
        run: curl --fail --location --ipv4 --retry 3 --output "${{ runner.temp }}/qwen2.5-0.5b-instruct-q4_k_m.gguf" https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct-GGUF/resolve/9217f5db79a29953eb74d5343926648285ec7e67/qwen2.5-0.5b-instruct-q4_k_m.gguf
      - name: Pretrained model comparisons with verified SHA-256 inputs
        env:
          LLAMA_TEST_MODEL: ${{ runner.temp }}/stories260K.gguf
          LLAMA_TEST_Q4_MODEL: ${{ runner.temp }}/stories15M-q4_0.gguf
          LLAMA_TEST_BPE_MODEL: ${{ runner.temp }}/SmolLM2-135M-Q4_K_M.gguf
          LLAMA_TEST_MAMBA_MODEL: ${{ runner.temp }}/mamba-130m-hf.f16.gguf
          LLAMA_TEST_QWEN2_MODEL: ${{ runner.temp }}/qwen2.5-0.5b-instruct-q4_k_m.gguf
          LLAMA_TEST_BERT_MODEL: ${{ runner.temp }}/bert-bge-small-f16.gguf
          LLAMA_TEST_BERT_BE_MODEL: ${{ runner.temp }}/bert-bge-small-f16-big-endian.gguf
        run: cargo test --release --offline --locked -p llama-inference -p llama-server --tests -- --ignored --nocapture
